html:
A Sumerian hymn to Ninkasi, the goddess of beer, written down on clay tablets about 1800 BCE. Its verses praise the goddess by describing how beer is made, so it doubles as one of the oldest recipes in the world.

The hymn follows the steps: baking bappir, a twice baked barley bread, soaking malt in jars, spreading the mash on mats to cool, and letting it ferment in a big vat before the beer pours out "like the onrush of the Tigris and Euphrates". In 1989 a California brewery brewed a beer from it.

Beer was a daily staple in the cities of Sumer and Babylonia. It was safer than much of the water, and workers were paid in rations of beer and bread. People drank it through straws to avoid the husks. The Code of Hammurabi has rules for women who kept taverns and sold beer, and cuneiform tablets list beer by the jar.
sum: A Sumerian hymn to Ninkasi, the goddess of beer, written down on clay tablets about 1800 BCE. Its verses praise the goddess by describing how beer is made, so it doubles as one of the oldest recipes in the world.
